key_insight: A context-aware Markov decision process can personalize Type 2 diabetes follow-up timing by risk subgroup instead of using one fixed interval for all patients.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help primary care teams schedule visits more efficiently, with shorter intervals for higher-risk patients and longer intervals for stable patients.
method: Used EHR data from 22,154 Type 2 diabetes patients across 10 primary care clinics.
Built patient contexts using principal component analysis plus clustering on trajectory and patient-level features.
Learned follow-up interval policies with a Contextual Markov Decision Process (CMDP).
evidence_signal: Compared with an ADA-like fixed-interval policy, the CMDP reduced expected cumulative cost by about 34.8% in the higher-comorbidity context and 6.4% in the lower-comorbidity context.
watch_item: The model depends on EHR quality and retrospective assumptions, so real-world implementation would need prospective validation before routine use.
paper_title: Context-Aware Optimization of Follow-Up Intervals for Type 2 Diabetes Care Using Markov Decision Processes
